description: await unwraps promises and passes plain values through
program: const f = async () => 41; [(await f()) + 1, await 5, await null]

description: an async function runs synchronously until its first await
program: const log = []; async function f() { log.push("a"); await null; log.push("c") } const p = f(); log.push("b"); await p; log

description: promise jobs run in FIFO order: an earlier then runs before a later await continuation
program: const log = []; Promise.resolve().then(() => log.push(1)); (async () => { await null; log.push(2) })(); await sleep(5); log

description: Promise.all keeps input order, not completion order, and accepts plain values
program: await Promise.all([sleep(20).then(() => "slow"), Promise.resolve("fast"), 3])

description: Promise.all of nothing resolves to []
program: await Promise.all([])

description: Promise.all rejects with the first rejection
program: let m; try { await Promise.all([Promise.resolve(1), Promise.reject(Error("bad")), sleep(5)]) } catch (e) { m = e.message } m

description: Promise.race settles with the first to settle
program: await Promise.race([sleep(50).then(() => "slow"), sleep(1).then(() => "fast")])

description: Promise.any fulfills with the first fulfilment, ignoring rejections
program: await Promise.any([Promise.reject(1), sleep(5).then(() => 2), sleep(30).then(() => 3)])

description: Promise.any rejects when everything rejects
program: let r = "no"; try { await Promise.any([Promise.reject(1), Promise.reject(2)]) } catch (e) { r = "rejected" } r

description: allSettled reports every outcome
program: await Promise.allSettled([Promise.resolve(1), Promise.reject("e")])

description: await of a rejected promise throws into try/catch
program: let m; try { await Promise.reject(Error("no")) } catch (e) { m = e.message } m

description: a throw inside an async function becomes a rejection
program: async function f() { throw Error("x") } await f().catch(e => "caught " + e.message)

description: then chains flatten returned promises
program: await Promise.resolve(1).then(x => x + 1).then(x => Promise.resolve(x * 10))

description: an exception in then reaches the next catch, which can recover
program: await Promise.resolve(1).then(() => { throw Error("t") }).catch(e => e.message + "!")

description: finally runs for both outcomes and passes the original value through
program: let n = 0; const v = await Promise.resolve(5).finally(() => { n++ }); let r; try { await Promise.reject(Error("z")).finally(() => { n++ }) } catch (e) { r = e.message } [v, r, n]

description: await inside loops runs sequentially
program: const out = []; for (const x of [3, 1, 2]) { out.push(await sleep(x).then(() => x)) } out

description: await may appear inside a template literal in an async function
program: const f = async () => `v=${await Promise.resolve(7)}`; await f()

description: map of async callbacks gives promises that Promise.all resolves
program: await Promise.all([1, 2, 3].map(async x => { await sleep(1); return x * 2 }))

description: sleep(ms) resolves to undefined after waiting
program: const t = await sleep(1); t === undefined

description: await inside a non-async function is a syntax error at the await
program: function f() { await 1 }

description: await inside a template of a non-async function is a syntax error
program: function f() { return `${await 1}` }

description: pmap maps with bounded parallelism and keeps order
program: await pmap([1, 2, 3, 4], async x => { await sleep(5 - x); return x * 2 }, {concurrency: 2})

description: stream(array) offers lazy transforms and terminals without processes
program: [await stream([1, 2, 3, 4]).filter(x => x % 2 === 0).map(x => x * 10).take(1).toArray(), await stream([1, 2, 3]).count()]
